clue.text: List without directions that can be believed

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the list stands round the compass points

parts.note: a table is a list or chart of items
E and N are the compass points east and north

explanation.surface: A list drawn up with no guidance turns out to be credible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of 'outside', not 'lacking'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenable position is one that can be defended or held, so it is credible.

clue.text: "Service" not permitted, they say, to militia

parts.note: a train is a rail service

indicators.note: they say signals that the words before it are heard rather than spelt

parts.note: not permitted means banned

explanation.surface: A rail service banned for the militia, according to rumour.
explanation.walkthrough: A train band was a citizen militia of the 17th and 18th centuries. The homophone covers only the second word.
explanation.definitionFit: Historical companies of trained citizen soldiers in London were called by this name, a militia.

clue.text: Basque country mostly in a stew

indicators.note: mostly means the region's name loses its final part

parts.note: Navarre is the Spanish region with a large Basque population

explanation.surface: Most of a Basque region finds itself in a state of agitation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' here drops the last two letters, RE, from NAVARRE; 'in a stew' looks like a state of worry but 'in' gives letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A navarin is a French ragout of mutton or lamb with root vegetables, a type of stew.

clue.text: See 1
English character nearly a heresy (Levellers' view)

indicators.note: nearly means the word for character stops one letter short

parts.note: a quality is a trait or character
Arianism, the fourth-century denial of Christ's full divinity, is a classic heresy

explanation.surface: An English temperament close to heresy, as the radical Levellers saw it.
explanation.walkthrough: The Levellers were radicals of the English Civil War who wanted equal rights for all; 'a' is a link word here.
explanation.definitionFit: The Levellers argued for political equality, which is the doctrine of equal rights for all citizens.

clue.text: Person said to take a pew, one attached to religion

indicators.note: said signals that the phrase after it is heard, not spelt

parts.note: to take a pew is a jokey British way to say sit down
I is the Roman numeral one
Zen is a school of Buddhism

explanation.surface: Someone told to sit down in church, a devout follower.
explanation.walkthrough: CIT, a old short form of citizen, sounds like SIT; 'attached to' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen is a person, especially an inhabitant of a town, as in Cowper's ballad.

clue.text: Change French boy's name to enter monarchy in good repute

indicators.note: to enter puts the following pieces inside the word for monarchy

parts.note: the Crown stands for the monarchy
to edit is to change a text
Andre is a French boy's name

explanation.surface: Altering a French lad's name to join the royal family wins him respect.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase comes from Cowper's comic ballad, whose hero is 'a citizen of credit and renown'.
explanation.definitionFit: To be held in credit and renown is to enjoy trust and fame, a good reputation.

clue.text: Relevance of current events to film on the new Italy

parts.note: a pic is a film or movie

indicators.note: new tells us the country's name is made afresh in another order

explanation.surface: Whether a news film about the modern Italy is up to date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns ITALY into ALITY; 'on' and 'the' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Topicality is the quality of dealing with matters of current interest, their relevance to the news.

clue.text: Spirit partly aroused by traveller

parts.note: zing is energy or spirit

indicators.note: partly says only some of the next word is taken, its opening letters

explanation.surface: Someone's spirit partly stirred up by a wanderer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' looks like a ghost or a drink, but here it is zest. ARO is the start of 'aroused'.
explanation.definitionFit: Zingaro is the Italian word for a gypsy, a member of a travelling people.

clue.text: Cup match on the isthmus could be a formality

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed below, so the match comes after

parts.note: a neck of land is a narrow isthmus
a cup tie is a knockout cup match

explanation.surface: A cup game played on a narrow strip of land between two seas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' says the definition is an example: a necktie is one formal item.
explanation.definitionFit: A necktie is worn for formal occasions, so it is one example of formal dress, a formality.

clue.text: Exploit a set containing 5

indicators.note: containing means the set of teeth holds the number inside it

parts.note: a denture is a set of false teeth
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: A heroic deed with a group holding a number.
explanation.walkthrough: '5' looks like a cross-reference to 5-across or 5-down, but it is simply the Roman numeral V.
explanation.definitionFit: An exploit is a daring deed, which is a synonym for an adventure.

clue.text: Godly fear

parts.note: read as fear sent by a god: the Greek god Pan was said to cause sudden terror in lonely places

explanation.walkthrough: The word comes from the Greek god Pan, whose sudden appearance spread terror.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudden overwhelming fright takes its name from the woodland god Pan, so fear from a god fits.

clue.text: Spy first of navigators with his ship

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: Noah, the first navigator in the Bible, sailed the ark

explanation.surface: A spy is the first sailor to own his boat.
explanation.walkthrough: The first navigator is Noah, so 'his ship' is the ark; 'with' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A nark is a police informer, someone who spies on others and reports to the authorities.

clue.text: Singing a little way into the factory

indicators.note: into means the short distance is put inside the factory word

parts.note: a plant is a factory
an inch is a small distance

explanation.surface: Songs heard as a person goes a short distance into a works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a little way' looks like a single phrase but gives two pieces: the article and the short distance.
explanation.definitionFit: Plainchant is unaccompanied church singing in unison, also called plainsong.

clue.text: 5 across of 5 down may be nigh during ragtime man's change of heart

indicators.note: during means the shuffled word is put inside the composer's name
change of heart means the middle letters of the name swap places

parts.note: Scott Joplin was the great composer of ragtime

indicators.note: may be suggests the letters of nigh may be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: Something close by while a ragtime composer changes his mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change of heart' swaps the central pair of the composer's name to make JOLPIN; 'may be' rearranges 'nigh', which goes in after the first two letters. Cowper's ballad calls its hero a citizen of credit and renown.
explanation.definitionFit: William Cowper's ballad describes its hero as a citizen of credit and renown, the answers to the cross-references.

clue.text: Fidgets, not love of walking

indicators.note: fidgets means the words that follow move restlessly into a new order

parts.note: love is nil in tennis scores, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A restless person who does not enjoy walking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fidgets' looks like the subject, but it is the anagram signal for NOT, O and OF.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on foot is to travel by walking rather than riding.

clue.text: Little lord in solitary, as said before use of gavel

definitions.text: as said before use of gavel

indicators.note: in means the short lord is placed inside the word for solitary

parts.note: solitary means alone
Ld is the abbreviation of lord

explanation.surface: A minor peer in solitary confinement, as the auctioneer cries before the hammer falls.
explanation.walkthrough: An auctioneer asks this just before bringing down the gavel to end bidding.
explanation.definitionFit: Auctioneers call this phrase, meaning bidding has finished, just before banging the hammer.

clue.text: This piggy went to market (writer to his sovereign)

parts.note: Francis Bacon was an Elizabethan essayist and writer
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the queen's royal cipher

explanation.surface: A nursery-rhyme piggy, and an author writing to his queen.
explanation.walkthrough: Francis Bacon served Elizabeth I, so the writer and sovereign fit together; 'to his' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A baconer is a pig fattened for bacon, sent to market like the nursery rhyme's little pig.

clue.text: Poet closes gap

definitions.meaning: Robert ... was Poet Laureate from 1913 to 1930
spans or joins across a gap, as a crossing over a river does

explanation.definitionFit: Robert Bridges the Laureate shares his surname with the verb for spanning a divide.

clue.text: Killer keeps fit: 13 was a 1 down 3 one

indicators.note: keeps means the murderer holds the word for fit inside him

parts.note: Cain killed his brother Abel in Genesis
apt means fit or suitable

explanation.surface: A murderer stays healthy, as John Gilpin was a militia officer.
explanation.walkthrough: Cowper's ballad says Gilpin 'a train-band captain eke was he'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gilpin held officer rank in the London militia, as the ballad's second line states.

clue.text: Remove heart from actor and replace with volunteers

indicators.note: heart from points at the central letter of the actor's name
replace with means that central letter is swapped for the volunteers

parts.note: Judi Dench is a celebrated British actor
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: Take out the heart of a performer and fill it with volunteers instead.
explanation.walkthrough: The central N of DENCH becomes TA.
explanation.definitionFit: To detach is to remove or separate one thing from another.

clue.text: Star changing place with US city

indicators.note: changing means the letters of place are rearranged

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: A celebrity swaps homes with an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' makes CAPEL from PLACE; 'with' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Capella is one of the brightest stars in the night sky, in the constellation Auriga.

clue.text: Involved with devil, spoke falsely, accepting punishment

parts.note: an imp is a little devil

indicators.note: accepting means the word for lied takes the punishment inside it

parts.note: to speak falsely is to lie
the cat o' nine tails was a whip used for punishment

explanation.surface: Someone mixed up with a demon told lies and was punished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link word; the cat o' nine tails is the punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: To be implicated is to be involved, especially in wrongdoing.

clue.text: Join together around piano and send out from the mouth

indicators.note: around means the stitching word goes round the musical letter

parts.note: to sew is to join with stitches
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: Stitching round a piano and then being sick.
explanation.definitionFit: To spew is to vomit or spit, sending matter out of the mouth.

clue.text: Refuse to be followed by 3, say?

indicators.note: say signals a word sounding like another

parts.note: the word that goes before band (3-down) to make the belt of a skirt is waist

explanation.surface: A rejection that will be followed by a cross-reference.
explanation.walkthrough: 3-down is BAND; waistband is the word, and WAIST sounds like WASTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Refuse as a noun means rubbish, which is waste.

clue.text: Top cards in tree

parts.note: the ace is the top card in many games
R, for Rex, is the king, another top card

explanation.surface: The best cards are hidden in a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The two highest cards are ace and king, and R (Latin rex) is the king; 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Acer is the botanical name for the maple genus of trees.

clue.text: Great snake suffering 'eat loss — comprehend?

indicators.note: suffering a loss of 'eat (heat with the h dropped) takes those letters from great

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake

explanation.surface: A big serpent feeling the heat, dropping its aitches, struggles to understand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eat is a Cockney heat; GREAT without EAT leaves GR.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp an idea is to comprehend it.

clue.text: Some celebrities in chaotic and unfinished session having one leg as long as the other?

definitions.text: having one leg as long as the other?

indicators.note: in means the celebrity fragment goes inside the jumbled session letters
chaotic means the letters are thrown into disorder
unfinished means the word loses its last letter
some says only part of the next word is used

explanation.surface: A few stars at a disorganised meeting that never finished, all legs of equal length.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' leaves SESSIO, which 'chaotic' rearranges round the three letters taken from 'celebrities'; the question mark marks the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An isosceles triangle has two sides, its legs, of equal length.

clue.text: Something wrong with love game, say? It comes to the same thing

definitions.text: It comes to the same thing

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: sin (something wrong) with O (love) and Nim (a game of taking counters) runs as sin-o-nim

explanation.surface: Is a tennis game with no score a sin?
explanation.walkthrough: Nim is a mathematical game of removing counters. Said aloud, SIN-O-NIM is heard as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A word with the same meaning as another word amounts to the same thing, an equivalent.

clue.text: Tell of return to alien island

indicators.note: return means the whole run of letters is read backwards

parts.note: ET is the film alien
Arran is an island in the Firth of Clyde, Scotland

explanation.surface: Relate the story of coming back to a foreign island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns ETARRAN into the answer; 'of' and 'to' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: To narrate is to tell a story or recount events.
